claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess this, I'll need to gather some information about your circumstances and any children you're responsible for.

Let me start with the first question:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do live in the UK. I'm asking because I have a 6-year-old, Alex, and I wanted to see if I can claim Child Benefit for them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! That's helpful to know.

Now, **are you the person who is responsible for looking after Alex?** This would typically mean either that you live with Alex, or that you're paying towards their care (such as food, clothes, pocket money, or accommodation).

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, Alex doesn't actually live with me - they live with their other parent. And to be honest, I'm not currently contributing financially towards their care.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I appreciate your honesty.

Based on what you've told me, it sounds like Alex lives with their other parent and you're not making financial contributions towards their care at the moment.

Before I give you a final answer, I just want to check one more thing:

**Have you had any arrangement or agreement (perhaps a court order or informal agreement) with the other parent about making payments towards Alex's upkeep or maintenance?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, there's no arrangement or court order in place. There's no agreement about me making payments for Alex's upkeep.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Summary:**

Unfortunately, you are **not currently eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex. 

Here's why: To qualify for Child Benefit, you need to be responsible for a child, which means either:
1. Living with them, or
2. Contributing financially to their care (food, clothes, pocket money, accommodation, etc.)

Since Alex lives with their other parent and you're not making financial contributions, you don't meet the eligibility requirements at this time.

However, this could change if your circumstances alter—for instance, if Alex were to come and live with you, or if you establish a formal arrangement to contribute towards their upkeep, you may become eligible. If that happens, you'd be able to make a new claim.

Is there anything else I can help you with?
